notice: Original starter questions; not official RSA questions. This is an early practice bank, not yet large enough for five full non-repeating exams. Check all legal details against current official sources.

topics.name: Road signs & signals
topics.note: Warning signs alert to hazards; regulatory signs impose requirements or prohibitions. A Garda direction takes precedence over traffic lights and signs.

topics.name: Rules of the road
topics.note: Drive on the left. Obey signs, signals, speed limits and road markings. Adapt speed to conditions and protect vulnerable road users.

topics.name: Vehicle checks & defects
topics.note: Check tyres, lights, mirrors, brakes, steering, fluids, wipers, coupling security and warning devices. Never use an unsafe vehicle.

topics.name: Loads & load security
topics.note: Never exceed plated weights or axle limits. Distribute weight evenly and secure it against movement.

topics.name: Trailers & couplings
topics.note: Confirm the coupling is compatible, fully engaged and locked. Check safety devices, trailer brakes, tyres and lights.

topics.name: Tachographs & drivers' hours
topics.note: Standard EU rules include 9 hours daily driving (10 hours twice weekly), 56 hours weekly and 90 hours over two weeks. After 4.5 hours driving, take 45 minutes break, splittable 15 then 30. Exemptions apply.

topics.name: Braking & stopping distances
topics.note: Stopping distance is thinking distance plus braking distance. Speed, mass, grip, gradient and brake condition affect it.

topics.name: Risk & eco-driving
topics.note: Scan ahead, anticipate hazards, maintain space and avoid harsh acceleration and braking. Fatigue and distraction increase risk.

topics.name: Dangerous goods
topics.note: ADR may regulate classification, packaging, marking, documents, equipment, training and exemptions. Check current ADR and Irish rules.

topics.name: Bus passenger safety
topics.note: Stop safely for boarding and alighting. Move only when doors are closed and passengers are safely accommodated.

topics.name: Vehicle dimensions & weight
topics.note: Know loaded height, width, length and permitted weights. Plan routes around restrictions and overhead clearances.

topics.name: Breakdowns & emergencies
topics.note: Protect people first, warn traffic when safe and follow emergency procedures. Call 112/999 for emergency assistance.

questions.question: A triangular warning sign generally means what?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are generally triangular; read the symbol and adjust speed.

questions.question: What does a red-bordered circular sign generally indicate?
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circular signs generally prohibit or restrict; the symbol gives the detail.

questions.question: A traffic signal changes to amber as you approach. What should you do?
options: Stop if you can do so safely
questions.explanation: Amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping could cause an accident.

questions.question: A Garda directs you to proceed while the signal is red. What should you do?
options: Follow the Garda's direction when safe
questions.explanation: A Garda's traffic direction takes precedence over traffic signals.

questions.question: You meet oncoming traffic on a narrow road. What is safest?
options: Slow and use a safe passing place if needed
Insist on priority because you are larger
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need extra room; pass only when safe and do not endanger pedestrians.

questions.question: A walk-around check reveals a deep cut in a tyre sidewall. What should you do?
options: Do not use the vehicle until repaired or assessed
questions.explanation: A damaged tyre can fail suddenly. Rectify roadworthiness defects before use.

questions.question: A brake warning light remains on before departure. What should you do?
options: Investigate and resolve the fault before driving
Ignore it if the parking brake is off
questions.explanation: A persistent brake warning may indicate a serious fault; follow manufacturer instructions.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of load restraint?
questions.explanation: Secure loads against braking, cornering and acceleration forces.

questions.question: A load is much heavier on one side. What is the main concern?
options: Uneven axle loading and reduced stability
No concern if total weight is legal
questions.explanation: Uneven distribution can overload an axle and adversely affect handling.

questions.question: Before moving with a trailer, what must be checked?
options: Coupling engaged and locked; connections secured
Only that the trailer looks level
Only that its registration is visible
questions.explanation: Check coupling, safety connections, brakes and lights before moving.

questions.question: Why connect a breakaway cable where fitted?
options: To activate emergency braking if trailer separates
questions.explanation: The safety device is intended to help stop a detached trailer; follow its instructions.

questions.question: Under standard EU rules, after how much driving is a 45-minute break normally required?
questions.explanation: A 45-minute break is required after 4.5 hours driving; it can be split 15 then 30 minutes.

questions.question: What is the normal daily driving limit under standard EU rules?
questions.explanation: Daily driving is normally 9 hours, extendable to 10 hours twice a week.

questions.question: What is the standard weekly driving limit under EU rules?
questions.explanation: Weekly driving is limited to 56 hours and 90 hours over two consecutive weeks.

questions.question: What can increase a heavy vehicle's stopping distance?
options: Higher speed and reduced tyre-road grip
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes reaction and braking distance; speed, grip, mass and gradient matter.

questions.question: What is a safer approach to a long steep descent?
options: Select a suitable low gear before descending
questions.explanation: A suitable gear and auxiliary braking help control speed and reduce brake overheating.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility. What should you do?
options: Reduce speed and increase following distance
Use high beam at all times
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance you can see to be clear.

questions.question: You feel drowsy while driving. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Fatigue impairs judgement and reaction; do not continue when unfit to drive.

questions.question: You cannot identify a potentially dangerous-goods package. What should you do?
options: Do not load until identified and requirements checked
questions.explanation: Dangerous goods must be correctly identified and handled under applicable ADR rules.

questions.question: When should a bus move away after passengers board?
options: When boarding is complete, doors closed and safe
As soon as first passenger boards
questions.explanation: Ensure doors are closed and passengers safely accommodated before moving.

questions.question: A passenger using a wheelchair boards. What is the priority?
options: Use the designated space and restraint system as instructed
questions.explanation: Use approved accessibility equipment and secure it in accordance with training.

questions.question: Your vehicle is higher than a bridge's signed clearance. What should you do?
options: Do not proceed; find another route
questions.explanation: Never attempt a route where the vehicle exceeds a height restriction.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down on a high-speed road. What comes first?
options: Protect people and get to safety if possible
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first; follow the road's breakdown procedure and seek help.
